question:
(a) Explain how total internal reflection is used in optical fibres.
(b) Why should the refractive index of the core of an optical fibre be greater than that of the cladding?
(c) Mention one practical use of optical fibres.

options.A:
(a) In optical fibres, light entering the core at a suitable angle strikes the core-cladding boundary at an angle greater than the critical angle and undergoes repeated total internal reflection, so it travels along the fibre.
(b) The core must have greater refractive index than the cladding so that light goes from denser to rarer medium at the boundary, satisfying the first condition for TIR.
(c) Optical fibres are used for long-distance signal transmission or as light pipes in medical instruments.
options.B:
(a) Optical fibres work by repeated refraction into the cladding.
(b) The cladding must have greater refractive index than the core.
(c) They are used only as heating elements.
options.C:
(a) Optical fibres work by reflection from a metallic coating.
(b) Core and cladding must have equal refractive indices to avoid bending.
(c) They are used to block light signals.
options.D:
(a) Total internal reflection occurs only when light travels from cladding to core.
(b) Hence the cladding must be optically denser.
(c) Optical fibres are used to reduce transmission distance.
